items.name: Cumin Whole-Wheat Roti
steps: Measure 190 ml (about 3/4 cup) warm water for Cumin Whole-Wheat Roti; begin with three quarters, then add the remainder by the tablespoon so the dough or batter does not become slack.
Knead the flour with cumin, salt, and warm water until supple. Knead for 8 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.
Rest the covered dough, then roll small rounds evenly. Keep the dough covered for 21–26 minutes, then roll on a lightly dusted surface to an even 2–3 mm thickness.
Preheat the griddle over medium heat for 7 minutes; a drop of water should skitter briefly and evaporate before the first bread goes on.

Cook each roti on a hot griddle and brush it lightly with ghee. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack the cooked breads under a clean cloth for 6 minutes so steam softens their surfaces; serve them warm rather than holding them on the griddle.

steps: Measure 190 ml (about 3/4 cup) warm water for Buckwheat Wheat Galette; begin with three quarters, then add the remainder by the tablespoon so the dough or batter does not become slack.

Whisk both flours with fennel, salt, oil, and water into batter. Whisk for 45–60 seconds until no flour pockets remain, then cover and rest the batter for 10 minutes before checking that it pours in a steady ribbon.
Rest briefly and pour a thin layer into the hot pan. Keep the dough covered for 15–20 minutes, then roll on a lightly dusted surface to an even 2–3 mm thickness.
For Buckwheat Wheat Galette, preheat the griddle over medium heat for 5 minutes; a drop of water should skitter briefly and evaporate before the first bread goes on.

Loosen the edge, turn once, and cook the second face lightly. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
For Buckwheat Wheat Galette, stack the cooked breads under a clean cloth for 8 minutes so steam softens their surfaces; serve them warm rather than holding them on the griddle.

items.name: Oat Wheat Griddle Flatbread

ingredients.name: Olive oil, divided for the griddle

steps: Measure 190 ml (about 3/4 cup) warm water for Oat Wheat Griddle Flatbread; begin with three quarters, then add the remainder by the tablespoon so the dough or batter does not become slack.
Combine oat and wheat flours with coriander and olive oil. Mix with the heat off for 45 seconds, lifting from the bottom until the ingredients are uniform and no clumps remain.
Knead with warm water, rest, and roll modest rounds. Knead for 7–8 minutes, keep the dough covered for 18–23 minutes, then roll on a lightly dusted surface to 2–3 mm.
For Oat Wheat Griddle Flatbread, preheat the griddle over medium heat for 6 minutes; a drop of water should skitter briefly and evaporate before the first bread goes on.

Cook on both faces until firm but still pliable. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
For Oat Wheat Griddle Flatbread, stack the cooked breads under a clean cloth for 5 minutes so steam softens their surfaces; serve them warm rather than holding them on the griddle.

items.name: Chickpea Olive Oil Socca

ingredients.name: Olive oil, divided for the griddle

steps: Measure 190 ml (about 3/4 cup) warm water for Chickpea Olive Oil Socca; begin with three quarters, then add the remainder by the tablespoon so the dough or batter does not become slack.
Whisk chickpea flour with cumin, salt, oil, and water. Whisk for 60 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.
Rest the thin batter while the heavy pan becomes hot. Keep the batter covered for 10 minutes, stir it for 20 seconds, and check that it falls from the ladle in a steady ribbon before spreading.
For Chickpea Olive Oil Socca, preheat the griddle over medium heat for 4 minutes; a drop of water should skitter briefly and evaporate before the first bread goes on.

Pour one broad layer and cook until set and browned underneath. Spread to about 3 mm thick and leave the first face undisturbed for 90–120 seconds, until the rim looks dry and small bubbles open across the top.
For Chickpea Olive Oil Socca, stack the cooked breads under a clean cloth for 5 minutes so steam softens their surfaces; serve them warm rather than holding them on the griddle.

items.name: Sesame Wheat Lavash

ingredients.name: Olive oil, divided for the griddle

steps: Measure 190 ml (about 3/4 cup) warm water for Sesame Wheat Lavash; begin with three quarters, then add the remainder by the tablespoon so the dough or batter does not become slack.
Knead the flour with oil, salt, and enough warm water. Knead for 7 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.
Roll rested portions paper-thin and scatter sesame over them. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.
For Sesame Wheat Lavash, preheat the griddle over medium heat for 6 minutes; a drop of water should skitter briefly and evaporate before the first bread goes on.

Press the seeds in and cook each sheet until crisp at the edges. Roll to an even 2–3 mm thickness, then cook over medium heat for 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until brown freckles reach the center.
Set the cooked sheets on a rack for 3 minutes without covering them; serve once the edges feel dry and crisp.
